blocks.en: D.2 eICU Dataset Processing
blocks.zh: D.2 eICU 数据集处理

blocks.en: The eICU Collaborative Research Database is a multi-center intensive care unit (ICU) database containing over 200,000 admissions from ICUs monitored by eICU programs in the United States [ Pollard et al., 2018 ] . It offers de-identified EHR data, encompassing demographics, diagnoses, treatments, and interventions. We use the eICU dataset to evaluate distribution shifts in patient observations across hospitals using both SMI and BioBERT embedding methods. We map diagnoses and medications to 72 unique integer-level ICD-9 codes and 241 unique five-level ATC codes. We treat each patient’s medical records as unordered observations without considering temporal order. We select the 10 hospitals with the largest number of patients, resulting in 2,418 patients per hospital and a total of 24,179 patients for analysis.
blocks.zh: eICU协作研究数据库是一个多中心重症监护单位(ICU)数据库,包含超过20万个受美国eICU方案监测的ICU的入院病例[Pollard等,2018]. 它提供非识别的EHR数据,包括人口统计、诊断、治疗和干预。 我们使用eICU数据集,使用SMI和BioBERT两种嵌入方法,来评价各医院患者观察的分布变化. 我们把诊断和药物映射到72个独特的整数级ICD-9编码和241个独特的五级ATC编码. 我们把每个病人的病历当作无序观察,而不考虑时间顺序。 我们选择了病人最多的10所医院,每所医院有2,418名病人,共有24,179名病人进行分析。

blocks.en: In eICU, approximately one-third of drug names are not recorded across the 208 hospitals (Fig. 6 a). This results in an extremely sparse input and thus hampers the model training due to the lack of informative features. To address this issue, we imputed the missing drug names using the Hierarchical Ingredient Code List (HICL) codes, a standardized coding system for healthcare products. Specifically, for entries without a drug name but with a HICL code, we retrieved the corresponding name by matching to other records that share the same HICL code and have a documented name. Using the HICL-based imputation strategy, the proportion of unrecorded drugs in our dataset was dropped to around 20% (Fig. 6 b), providing denser medication inputs for downstream modeling.
blocks.zh: 在eICU中,大约三分之一的药物名称没有记录到208所医院(图6a)。 这导致投入极为稀少,因此由于缺乏信息性特征,阻碍了模式培训。 为了解决这一问题,我们使用保健产品标准化编码系统“分级成份编码清单”(HICL)来估算缺失的药物名称。 具体地说,对于没有药物名称但有HICL代码的条目,我们通过与其它共享HICL代码并有文件记载名称的记录相匹配而检索出相应的名称. 使用基于HICL的估算策略,我们数据集中未录入的药物比例下降到了20%左右(图6b),为下游建模提供了更密集的药物投入.

blocks.en: Figure 6: The drug rates before and after imputation of the eICU data. Since some drugs may lack recorded names, drug rates indicate the proportion of administered drugs with recorded names over all unique drugs.
blocks.zh: 图 6:eICU数据估算前后的毒品率. 由于有些药物可能缺乏有记录的名称,因此药物比率表明有记录名称的所服用药物在所有独特药物中所占比例。

blocks.en: Drug names in eICU are recorded as free-text strings with dosage information, units, and other administration-related details. Consequently, the same active ingredient can appear in many lexical variants, potentially introducing irrelevant noise for training. To address this issue, we applied a data cleaning procedure to the drug-name strings. Specifically, we retained the tokens corresponding to the core medications and removed administration-specific details such as dosages, units, and numeric values. The resulting drug texts more closely reflect the medication’s active-ingredient terms, supporting more stable and transferable medication representations.
blocks.zh: eICU中的药物名称被记录为有剂量信息,单位,以及其他行政相关细节的自由文本串. 因此,同样的活性成分可能出现在许多词汇的变体中,有可能为培训带来无关的噪音。 为了解决这个问题,我们对药物名称串采用了数据清理程序。 具体地说,我们保留了与核心药物对应的代号,并删除了特定疗效的细节,如剂量,单位和数值等. 由此产生的药物文本更密切地反映了药物的积极耐受性,支持更加稳定和可转移的药物说明。

blocks.en: We also found that the same medication can appear under different names in the eICU dataset (e.g., trade/brand names vs. ingredient names), creating multiple lexical variants of the same drug entity. This variability inflates the effective vocabulary and introduces spurious distinctions that reduce model robustness. To mitigate this issue, we harmonized eICU drug strings by mapping them to standardized medication concepts using the WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification system. Specifically, we first collected ATC classes from the WHO Collaborating Centre for Drug Statistics Methodology website [ Kury, 2024 ] . We then leveraged the five-level ATC hierarchy and extracted the 5th-level ATC substance codes as well as their descriptions. For each eICU canonical drug name, we computed BioWordVec embeddings using for both the eICU string and each reference ATC substance name [ Zhang et al., 2019 ] . We then measured the cosine similarity between these two word embeddings. After comparing with all reference drug names, the reference ATC substance name with the highest cosine similarity is selected. We also assigned the corresponding ATC code to each medication record. This procedure effectively matches drugs with similar ATC codes, improves the consistency of medication concepts across records, and supports standardized analyses across ATC levels.
blocks.zh: 我们还发现,同样的药物可以在eICU数据集的不同名称下出现(例如:贸易/品牌名称与成份名称),从而形成同一种药物实体的多语法变体. 这种可变性夸大了有效的词汇并引入了会降低模型稳健性的虚假区分. 为了减轻这一问题,我们利用卫生组织的解剖治疗化学分类系统,将eICU药物串与标准化药物概念相协调。 具体而言,我们首先从世卫组织药物统计方法合作中心网站[Kury,2024]收集了ATC课程。 然后我们利用了5级ATC等级,提取出5级ATC物质代码及其描述. 对于每一个eICU的克能克药物名称,我们计算出BioWordVec嵌入物,同时使用eICU字符串和每个参考ATC物质名称[张等,2019]. 然后我们测量了这两个词嵌入的同位素相似性。 与所有参考药物名称相提并论后,选择了余弦相似度最高的参考ATC物质名称. 我们还为每一个药物记录分配了相应的ATC代码. 这一程序有效地将药物与类似的ATC代码相匹配,提高了各种记录的药物概念的一致性,并支持跨ATC级别的标准化分析.

blocks.en: D.3 Prompt for Biomedical LMs
blocks.zh: D.3. 生物医学遗留物的迅速处理

blocks.en: Specifically, we use a frozen Biomedical LM model as an encoder. For each medical concept, we first generate the description of the clinical code at every level and explicitly concatenate its full hierarchical path, incorporating the descriptions of all ancestor codes in the hierarchy. We find that the hierarchy-aware input is more effective in capturing medical semantics. Table 9 presents the BioBERT input prompt, in which the text passed to the LM encoder explicitly encodes the hierarchical context of a clinical concept.
blocks.zh: 具体来说,我们使用冷冻生物医学LM模型作为编码器. 对于每一个医学概念,我们首先生成各级临床密码的描述,并明确凝聚其完整的分级路径,将所有祖先密码的描述纳入分级. 我们发现,分级意识输入在捕捉医学语义方面更为有效. 表9列出了BioBERT输入快取,其中转至LM编码器的文本明确编码了临床概念的分级上下文.

blocks.en: Table 9: Level-specific textual descriptions used by the biomedical LM. The example includes an ICD-10 diagnosis ( I15.1 Hypertension secondary to other renal disorders ), an ICD-10 procedure ( 79658 Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of Lumbar Spine ), and an ATC medication ( A10AE04 Insulin glargine ). For each hierarchy level, we encode only the textual description of the code at that level, rather than concatenating descriptions along the full ontology path.
blocks.zh: 表9:生物医学LM使用的具体级别文字描述. 例子包括ICD-10诊断(I15.1高血压次于其他肾功能障碍),ICD-10程序(Lumbar Spine的79658磁共振成像(MRI))和ATC药物(A10AE04 Insulin glargine). 对于每个层次,我们只编码该层次代码的文字描述,而不是沿着完整的本体学路径来整理描述.

blocks.en: D.4 Baseline Details
blocks.zh: D.4 基线细节

blocks.en: We compare SMI against representative baseline methods for learning medical concept embeddings. These baselines differ in how they incorporate textual information, ontology structure, and embedding geometry, providing complementary points of comparison for evaluating hierarchy awareness and robustness under long-tailed concept distributions. We include both concept-level and patient-level representation baselines, as several prior clinical models derive concept embeddings implicitly through task-driven training.
blocks.zh: 我们比较SMI与具有代表性的学习医学概念嵌入的基线方法. 这些基线在如何纳入文字信息、肿瘤结构以及嵌入几何方面各不相同,为在长尾概念分布下评价等级意识和稳健性提供了互补的比较点。 我们既包括概念层面的代表基线,也包括病人层面的代表基线,因为一些先前的临床模型通过任务驱动的培训,隐含了概念嵌入。

blocks.en: BioBERT encodes clinical concepts by embedding their textual descriptions using a pretrained biomedical language model [ Lee et al., 2020 ] , yielding hierarchy-agnostic Euclidean representations. While effective for frequent concepts, BioBERT does not explicitly model hierarchical relationships among medical codes and tends to degrade for sparse, fine-grained concepts.
blocks.zh: BioBERT通过使用被预先训练的生物医学语言模型来嵌入其文字描述来编码临床概念[Lee等,2020年],产生层次-不可知的欧几利得表述. BioBERT虽然对频繁的概念有效,但并没有明确地在医疗代码之间树立等级关系的模式,而且往往会因零散而细微的概念而退化.

blocks.en: SapBERT learns biomedical concept representations by aligning synonymous terms in UMLS using contrastive learning over pretrained biomedical language models [ Liu et al., 2021 ] . By enforcing proximity among synonym sets, SapBERT improves semantic consistency and entity normalization performance. However, its supervision is limited to local synonym relations and does not explicitly model hierarchical or multi-level ontology structure, making it insufficient for preserving coarse-to-fine semantics across medical taxonomies.
blocks.zh: SapBERT通过校正UMLS中的同义词来学习生物医学概念表述,使用对比性学习而不是预先训练的生物医学语言模型[刘等,2021]. 通过在同义词集之间强制相近,SapBERT提高了语义一致性和实体正常化性能. 然而,其监督仅限于当地同义词关系,没有明确的模拟分级或多层次的肿瘤结构,使其不足以保存整个医学分类学的粗到细的语义.

blocks.en: G-BERT incorporates medical ontology information into a Transformer model by augmenting patient records with graph-based contextual representations and pretraining objectives [ Shang et al., 2019 ] . While effective for medication recommendation, G-BERT focuses on patient-level sequence modeling and does not produce standalone hierarchy-aware concept embeddings.
blocks.zh: G-BERT将医学本体学信息纳入"变形器"模型,通过以图表为基础的上下文表述和预训目标来扩充患者记录[Sang等,2019]. G-BERT虽然对药物推荐有效,但专注于患者级别的序列建模,并不产生独立的层次意识概念嵌入.

blocks.en: HiTs treats pretrained language models as implicit hierarchy encoders by supervising them to produce representations that respect hierarchical relations among concepts [ He et al., 2024 ] . While effective at aligning LM embeddings with taxonomic structure through structured objectives, HiTs relies on learning hierarchy consistency during training and does not explicitly aggregate multi-level ancestor context to form a single coarse-to-fine concept embedding.
blocks.zh: HiTs将预训语言模型作为隐含的分级编码器,通过监督它们产生尊重概念间分级关系的表示[. He et al., 2024] (英语). HiTs虽然通过结构化目标有效地使LM嵌入结构与分类结构相协调,但在培训期间依赖于学习层次的一致性,并且没有明确汇总多层次祖先上下文形成单一粗到细的概念嵌入.

blocks.en: OnT treats pretrained language models as ontology encoders by fine-tuning them under geometric constraints in hyperbolic space to preserve logical relations defined in OWL ontologies [ Yang et al., 2025 ] . By jointly incorporating textual labels and formal ontology axioms, OnT achieves strong hierarchy consistency and supports ontology-level reasoning tasks. In contrast to SMI, OnT focuses on enforcing global logical structure through geometric modeling, rather than aggregating multi-level semantic signals along ontology paths for downstream clinical representation learning.
blocks.zh: OnT将预训语言模型作为肿瘤编码器,在双曲空间的几何限制下对其进行微调,以保留OWL肿瘤所定义的逻辑关系[杨等,2025]. OnT通过联合融合了文字标签和正式的本体学动因子,实现了强烈的层次一致性,并支持本体学级推理任务. 与SMI形成对比的是,OnT专注于通过几何模型执行全球逻辑结构,而不是将多层次的语义信号沿着肿瘤路径汇总,用于下游临床表现学习.

blocks.en: GRAM learns medical concept representations by recursively aggregating ancestor information in a medical ontology using an attention mechanism [ Choi et al., 2017 ] . By leveraging hierarchical structure, GRAM improves embeddings for rare concepts, but it is trained in a supervised, task-specific manner rather than producing general-purpose concept embeddings.
blocks.zh: GRAM学习医学概念表达,通过递归式地将祖先信息汇总到医学肿瘤学中,使用关注机制[Choi等,2017]. 通过利用分级结构,GRAM改进了稀有概念的嵌入,但是它以监督,任务特定的方式培训,而不是产生通用概念嵌入.

blocks.en: cui2vec learns distributed embeddings of medical concepts by applying word embedding methods to large-scale clinical notes, claims data, and biomedical literature [ Beam et al., 2020 ] . These embeddings capture statistical co-occurrence patterns but do not explicitly encode hierarchical or relational structure from medical ontologies.
blocks.zh: cui2vec通过对大规模临床笔记,索赔数据,以及生物医学文献等应用词嵌入法来学习分布式嵌入医学概念[Beam等,2020]. 这些嵌入法捕捉统计共生规律,但并没有从医学本体学中明确编码分级或关系结构.

blocks.en: RotatE embeds entities in complex space and models relations as rotations, enabling it to capture symmetry, antisymmetry, and inversion patterns in knowledge graphs [ Sun et al., 2019 ] . While more expressive than TransE, RotatE does not explicitly encode hierarchical depth or ontology-defined parent–child semantics.
blocks.zh: 罗塔特 E将实体嵌入复杂的空间和模型关系作为旋转,使其能够在知识图中捕捉对称,反对称和倒置模式[. Sun等, 2019] (中文(中国大陆) ). RotatE虽然比TransE更具表达性,但没有明确编码等级深度或本体学定义的亲子语义.

blocks.en: BEHRT is a Transformer-based model pretrained on longitudinal EHR sequences using diagnosis codes, age, and temporal embeddings to learn patient representations [ Li et al., 2020 ] . While effective for clinical risk prediction, BEHRT is designed for patient-level modeling rather than reusable medical concept embeddings.
blocks.zh: BEHRT是一个基于变形器的模型,在纵向EHR序列上预先训练,使用诊断代码,年龄,和时间嵌入来学习病人的表示 [Li等,2020]. 虽然BEHRT对临床风险预测有效,但它是针对患者一级模型设计,而不是重复使用的医学概念嵌入.

blocks.en: Med-BERT pretrains a BERT-style model on structured EHR data using masked code prediction and visit-level objectives to capture medical context [ Rasmy et al., 2021 ] . Although Med-BERT improves downstream clinical tasks, it focuses on contextual patient representations rather than explicit hierarchy-aware concept encoding.
blocks.zh: Med-BERT在结构化的EHR数据上预留了一种BERT式模型,使用蒙面代码预测和访问级目标来捕捉医疗背景[Rasmy等,2021]. 尽管Med-BERT改进了下游的临床任务,但它侧重于上下文的病人表现,而不是明确的分级意识概念编码.

blocks.en: ClinicalBERT adapts BERT to the clinical domain by pretraining on MIMIC clinical notes to learn contextualized representations of medical language [ Alsentzer et al., 2019 ] . These embeddings capture rich clinical semantics from text but do not explicitly encode medical ontologies or hierarchical relations among concepts.
blocks.zh: 临床BERT通过MIMIC临床笔记的预训来使BERT适应临床领域,以学习医学语言的上下文表述[Alsentzer等,2019]. 这些嵌入语从文本中捕捉出丰富的临床语义,但没有明确编码医学本体或概念之间的分级关系.

blocks.en: BERGAMOT learns biomedical entity representations by combining LM-based concept encoding with graph-augmented representation learning [ Sakhovskiy et al., 2024 ] . It jointly leverages textual concept information and biomedical graph structure to improve entity representations. This requires additional graph-based representation learning and does not explicitly construct a coarse-to-fine concept representation by aggregating level-specific embeddings along an expert-defined ontology path.
blocks.zh: BERGAMOT通过将基于LM的概念编码与图化的表示学习相结合来学习生物医学实体的表示[Sakhovskiy等,2024]. 它联合利用文字概念信息和生物医学图表结构来改进实体的表述. 这就需要更多的基于图表的表达学习,并且没有通过在专家定义的本体学路径上汇总不同层次的嵌入来明确构建粗到细的概念表达.

blocks.en: BoxLM is a recent ontology-aware clinical prediction model that combines LM-based semantic representations with box embeddings to capture hierarchical structure for diagnosis prediction [ Tan et al., 2025 ] . It represents medical concepts using box geometry and incorporates ontology-driven structure into a task-specific prediction framework. BoxLM is optimized for supervised prediction and does not provide a training-free, task-agnostic concept representation constructed from frozen LM embeddings along ontology paths.
blocks.zh: BoxLM是一种近期的本体学-认知临床预测模型,将基于LM的语义表达法和箱嵌入法结合起来,以捕捉分级结构来进行诊断预测[Tan等,2025]. 它代表了使用框几何的医学概念,并将本体学驱动的结构纳入任务特定预测框架. BoxLM被优化用于有监督的预测,不提供从被冻结的LM嵌入到肿瘤路径上构建的无培训,任务不可知的概念表述.

blocks.en: D.5 Computational resources
blocks.zh: D.5 计算资源

blocks.en: All experiments were conducted on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU with 96GB memory. SMI is training-free and only requires a one-time computation of frozen LM embeddings, after which the embeddings are reused in downstream tasks. Therefore, SMI introduces minimal additional hardware or computational overhead beyond the baseline embedding extraction and downstream evaluation.
blocks.zh: 所有实验都是在具有96GB内存的NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU上进行的. SMI是无培训的,只需要一次性地计算被冻结的LM嵌入物,之后再将嵌入物再用于下游任务. 因此,SMI在基准嵌入提取和下游评价之外引入了最低限度的额外硬件或计算间接费用。

blocks.en: Appendix E Additional Results
blocks.zh: 附录E 其他结果

blocks.en: E.1 Long Tail Distribution of Clinical Concepts
blocks.zh: E.1 临床概念的长尾分布

blocks.en:
Figure 7: Rank–frequency distributions (log–log scale) of clinical concepts in MIMIC-IV across five hierarchy levels:
(a) ICD-9 diagnosis codes, (b) ICD-9 procedure codes, and (c) ATC medication codes.
For each hierarchy level, concepts are ranked by patient frequency within that level.
blocks.zh:
图7:MIMIC-IV的临床概念在五个层次的排名-频率分布(log-log规模):
(a) ICD-9诊断代码,(b) ICD-9程序代码,(c) ATC药物代码。
对于每个等级级别,概念都按该等级范围内的病人频率排序.

blocks.en: Clinical concepts in EHRs typically exhibit highly skewed, long-tailed distributions: a small subset of clinical codes appear frequently, while most codes are observed with low frequencies. To quantify this pattern in MIMIC-IV dataset, we compute patient-level frequencies for three coding systems: ICD-9 diagnoses, ICD-9 procedures, and ATC medications. For each hierarchy, we measure the number of unique patients associated with each concept at all five levels, rank concepts by frequency, and plot the resulting rank–frequency curves on log–log scales.
blocks.zh: EHRs中的临床概念通常表现出高度扭曲的长尾分布:临床代码的一小部分经常出现,而大多数代码的观测频率低. 为了在MIMIC-IV数据集中量化这个模式,我们计算出三个编码系统的病人水平频率:ICD-9诊断,ICD-9程序,ATC药物. 对于每个等级,我们在所有五个级别上衡量与每个概念有关的独特病人的数量,按频率排列概念,并在log-log比例尺上绘制由此产生的等级-频率曲线。

blocks.en: Fig. 7 summarizes the rank–frequency distributions across hierarchy levels for ICD-9 diagnoses, ICD-9 procedures, ATC medications. A consistent long-tail pattern emerges in all three hierarchies: coarse-grained levels include fewer concepts with higher patient frequencies, whereas fine-grained levels contain many more concepts whose frequencies drop sharply, yielding a large fraction of rare codes. This significant sparsity at fine granularity makes it difficult for hierarchy-agnostic LM embeddings to learn meaningful representations from limited observations. These results motivate hierarchy-aware SMI approach that integrates expert-defined hierarchical semantics to improve representations for infrequent, fine-grained clinical concepts.
blocks.zh: 图7总结了ICD-9诊断、ICD-9程序、ATC药物的分级频率分布。 在所有三个分级中都出现了一贯的长尾图案:粗细分级包含的患者频率较高的概念较少,而细长分级包含更多的,其频率急剧下降,产生一大部分稀有代码. 这种在细颗粒性上具有显著的伸缩性,使得分层-不可知LM嵌入器难以从有限的观测中学习有意义的表达. 这些结果激励了具有分级意识的SMI方法,该方法融合了专家定义的分级语义,以改善不常见,精细的临床概念的表述.

blocks.en: E.2 Details about Clinical Relation Prediction
blocks.zh: E.2 临床关系预测的细节

blocks.en:
We design our multi-hop prediction task within the ICD and ATC hierarchies following the setup of prior work [ Ganea et al., 2018 ] . The goal is to evaluate whether the model can infer indirect, multi-hop subsumption relations from direct, one-hop subsumptions. For each positive pair where one concept subsumes another, we sample 10 negative parent candidates that are not connected to the child concept via either direct or indirect subsumption, leading to 10 training triplets per positive example
We consider two negative-sampling strategies: (1) hard negatives, chosen from sibling concepts (i.e., concepts sharing the same parent); (2) random negatives, uniformly from the remaining concepts. When a concept has fewer than 10 siblings, we fill in with random negatives to maintain 1-to-10 ratio of positives to negatives.
blocks.zh:
我们设计了在ICD和ATC的分级内进行多跳预测的任务,之前的工作设置[Ganea等,2018]. 目标是评价模型是否能够从直接,一跳子假设中推断出间接,多跳子的子假设关系. 对于一个概念包含另一个概念的每对阳性对子,我们抽取了10名与儿童概念没有关联的阳性父母候选人,通过直接或间接的分接,导致每个阳性对子进行10次培训
我们考虑两种负面抽样策略:(1)从同父异母概念(即共享同母概念)中选择的硬底片;(2)随机底片,从其余概念中统一. 当一个概念的兄弟姐妹少于10个时,我们填写随机的负数,以保持正数与负数的1-10比.

blocks.en: For cross-ontology relation prediction [ Zou et al., 2022 ] , we evaluate a one-hop relation prediction using ICD → \rightarrow ATC-10 pair. Given an ATC medication code, we predict whether a candidate ICD-10 diagnosis code is linked to it. Since each ATC maps to a single ICD-10 label in our dataset, we restrict evaluation to 1-hop prediction and sample one negative ICD-10 code per positive pair.
blocks.zh: 对于交叉肿瘤关系预测[Zou等,2022],我们用ICD →\右旋ATC-10对来评价一跃关系预测. 鉴于ATC药物代码,我们预测候选的ICD-10诊断代码是否与之相关. 由于每个ATC的映射到我们数据集的单个ICD-10标签,我们把评价限制在1-hop的预测上,并抽取每正对一个负的ICD-10代码.

blocks.en: For both multi-hop prediction within the ICD and ATC hierarchies and the cross-ontology one-hop ICD → \rightarrow ATC task, we report Precision, Recall, and F-score as the evaluation metrics. We do not use accuracy metric because class imbalance can inflate it; as the large number of negatives can cause misleadingly high scores.
blocks.zh: 对于ICD和ATC等级内的多跳预测和交叉肿瘤学一跳ICD ~\右旋ATC任务,我们把精度,回想和F分数作为评价的衡量标准. 我们没有使用精确度测量标准,因为阶级不平衡会加剧它;因为大量的负数会造成误导性的高分.

blocks.en: E.3 Details about Clustering Analysis
blocks.zh: E.3 分组分析的细节

blocks.en:
We evaluate how well the embeddings group clinical codes into highest-level clinical group (i.e., major categories for ICD diagnostic and procedure codes, and Anatomical main groups for ATC medication codes). To do so, we apply K-means clustering to both BioBERT and SMI embeddings, setting the number of clusters K K to match the number of ground-truth categories. We evaluate clustering quality using three groups of metrics: (1) Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), and Purity measure cluster-label alignment with ICD major categories; (2) Per-category Recall and Precision measure how coherently each major category is grouped and how pure its dominant cluster is; (3) Silhouette and Intra/Inter Ratio measure whether embeddings from the same major category are compact and separated from other categories.
For all three metric groups, we report the aggregate clustering results in Table 10 . For per-category Recall and Precision across the 18 ICD major categories, we report detailed results in Table 11 .
blocks.zh:
我们评价将群体临床代码嵌入最高水平的临床组(即ICD诊断和程序代码的主要类别,以及ATC药物代码的解剖学主要组别)。 为此,我们在BioBERT和SMI嵌入物中都应用了K-意指集群,设定了集群K K的数量来匹配地真类的数量. 我们利用三组衡量标准评价分组质量: (1) 规范化的相互信息、调整后Rand指数和纯度衡量集群标签与ICD主要类别的一致性;(2) 逐类回顾和精确度衡量每个主要类别如何连贯地分类,其主导类别如何纯度;(3) 衡量同一主要类别的嵌入是否紧凑并与其他类别相分离。
对所有三个计量组而言,我们在表10中报告汇总分组结果。 对于18个国际疾病分类主要类别的每个类别,我们将在表11中报告详细结果。

blocks.en: We first report global clustering metrics that evaluate how well the unsupervised clusters align with ICD major categories. Specifically, we use NMI, ARI, and cluster Purity. NMI measures the mutual information agreement between cluster assignments and major-category labels. ARI measures pairwise agreement between the clustering result and the ground-truth labels after correcting for chance. Purity measures the fraction of samples in each cluster that belong to its dominant major category. Higher values indicate stronger ontology-consistent clustering.
blocks.zh: 我们首先报告全球分组衡量标准,用以评价无监督的分组如何与国际疾病分类主要类别保持一致。 具体来说,我们使用NMI,ARI,和集群纯度。 NMI衡量集群任务与主要类别标签之间的相互信息协议. ARI测量分组结果与地面真实标签之间的对等协议,然后纠正机会。 纯度测量每个集群中属于其主要类别样本的分量。 较高的数值表明,本体学与本体学一致的集群更强.

blocks.en: We next report Recall and Precision to evaluate category-level clustering quality. For each ICD major category, we compute per-category Recall and Precision, and then report their macro-averages as aggregate metrics in Table 10 . Detailed per-category results are reported in Table 11 . Let c c index the resulting clusters, and let c ∗ ​ ( m ) c^{\ast}(m) denote the dominant cluster for category m m , defined as the cluster containing the largest number of codes from m m .
blocks.zh: 下一份报告回顾和精确评价分类分组的质量。 对于每个ICD主要类别,我们计算每个类别召回和精确度,然后在表10中将其宏观平均值作为总指标报告。 每个类别的详细结果见表11。 让 c 指数化生成的集群,让 c 表示 m 类的主导集群,定义为含有 m m 代码数最多的集群。

blocks.en: Per-category Recall measures how well a diagnostic major m m is captured by a single cluster. It is , it defined as the proportion of ICD codes from major m m that are assigned to its dominant cluster c ∗ ​ ( m ) c^{\ast}(m) : recall ⁡ ( m ) = P ⁡ ( cluster = c ∗ ​ ( m ) ∣ major = m ) \mathrm{recall}(m)=P(\text{cluster}=c^{*}(m)\mid\text{major}=m) Higher Recall indicates that codes from the same major category are concentrated in one coherent cluster, while lower Recall indicates that the category is scattered across multiple clusters.
blocks.zh: 按类别 回顾衡量一个诊断性主要 m m 被一个集群所捕获的程度。 它被定义为主要 m m 的ICD 代码中分配给其主要集群 c ( m) c ( s) ( m):  recall (m) = P ⁡ (组数 = c * (m) += m)\ mathrm{ recall} (m)=P(\text{组数 +c^{*}(m)\mid\text{major}) 较高的召回表示,来自同一主要类别的代码集中在一个连贯的集群,而较低的召回表示该类别分散在多个集群.

blocks.en: Per-category Precision measures the purity of the dominant cluster corresponding to a diagnostic major m m . It is defined as the proportion of ICD codes within the dominant cluster c ∗ ​ ( m ) c^{*}(m) that belong to major m m : precision ⁡ ( m ) = P ⁡ ( major = m ∣ cluster = c ∗ ​ ( m ) ) \mathrm{precision}(m)\;=\;P\bigl(\text{major}=m\mid\text{cluster}=c^{\ast}(m)\bigr) Higher Precision indicates that the dominant cluster contains few codes from other major categories, while lower Precision indicates stronger mixing across categories.
blocks.zh: 每类精度测量与诊断主要 m相对应的主要群的纯度。 它被定义为主流集群c* (m) c^{*} (m) 中属于主要 m:精度  (m) = P⁡ (major = m ∣ (c) )\ mathrm{精度} (m)\;\;\;P\bigl (\text{major}=m\mid\text{ cluster_c^{\ast} (m)\biger) 高精度表示主流集群中包含从其他主要类别中取出很少的代码,而更低精度表示各类别更强的混合.

blocks.en: We also report Silhouette score and Intra/Inter Ratio as global embedding-space separation metrics to assess whether ICD major categories are geometrically separated. Silhouette score measures whether each code is closer to codes in its own cluster than to codes in other clusters, where higher values indicate better separation. Intra/Inter Ratio is defined as the average within-major-category distance divided by the average between-major-category distance. Lower values indicate more compact embeddings within the same major category and stronger separation across different major categories.
blocks.zh: 我们还将Silhouette分数和内部/内部比率作为全球嵌入-空间分离指标,以评估国际疾病分类主要类别是否几何分离。 Silhouette分数衡量每个代码是否更接近于自身集群中的代码,而不是其他集群中的代码,其中较高的值表示更好的分离. 内部/内部比率被定义为主要类别内平均距离除以主要类别间平均距离。 较低的数值表明,在同一主要类别内嵌入的更紧凑,不同主要类别间更紧密地分开。

blocks.en: Table 10 shows that SMI improves cluster-label alignment over BioBERT, with higher NMI (0.77 vs. 0.39), ARI (0.56 vs. 0.25), and Purity (0.78 vs. 0.51). This indicates that the clusters induced by SMI embeddings are more consistent with ICD major disease categories. SMI also improves per-category clustering quality, achieving higher average Recall (0.80 vs. 0.41) and Precision (0.61 vs. 0.35), showing that codes from the same major category are grouped more coherently and that the dominant clusters are less mixed with codes from other categories. Table 11 further shows that this improvement holds across most ICD major categories. Finally, SMI improves embedding-space separation, with a higher Silhouette score (0.52 vs. 0.04) and a lower Intra/Inter Ratio (0.29 vs. 0.82), indicating that codes within the same major category are more compact while different major categories are better separated. Overall, these results support that SMI produces diagnosis embeddings that are more aligned with the ICD ontology than BioBERT embeddings.
blocks.zh: 表10显示,SMI比BioBERT改进了集群标签的配比,NMI更高(0.77对0.39)、ARI更高(0.56对0.25)和Purity更纯正(0.78对0.51)。 这表明由SMI嵌入所诱发的集群与ICD主要疾病类别更为一致. SMI还提高了每类集群的质量,实现了更高的平均召回(0.80对0.41)和精密(0.61对0.35),表明同一主要类别的代码被更一致地分组,主导类集群与其他类别代码的混合较少. 表11还表明,这一改善适用于大多数国际疾病分类的主要类别。 最后,SMI改进了嵌入-空间分离,Silhouette分数较高(0.52对0.04),内部/内部比更低(0.29对0.82),这表明同一类主要类别的代码比较紧凑,而不同的主要类别则更好地分离. 总体而言,这些结果支持SMI产生比BioBERT嵌入更符合国际疾病肿瘤学的诊断嵌入.

blocks.en: Table 10: Aggregate clustering quality of ICD diagnosis embeddings by major disease category. NMI, ARI, Purity, Recall, Precision, and Silhouette are higher better, while Intra/Inter Ratio is lower better. SMI achieves stronger cluster-label alignment and better geometric separation than BioBERT, indicating more ontology-consistent diagnosis embeddings.
blocks.zh: 表10:按主要疾病类别分列的国际疾病诊断嵌入物的集合质量。 NMI、ARI、纯度、召回、精度和Silhouette都较好,而内部/内部比率则较好。 SMI比BioBERT实现更强的集群-标签对接并更好的几何分化,表明更多的本体-一致的诊断嵌入.

blocks.en: Table 11: Per-major clustering recall and precision by ICD major disease category. Recall measures whether codes from the same major category are concentrated in a dominant cluster, while precision measures the purity of that dominant cluster. SMI achieves higher recall and precision than BioBERT for most ICD major categories, indicating more coherent and less mixed ontology-aligned clusters.
blocks.zh: 表11:按疾病分类主要疾病类别分列的每类主要群体召回和准确性。 回顾关于同一主要类别的编码是否集中在一个主导集群,而精确度衡量该主导集群的纯度。 SMI在大多数ICD主要类别中比BioBERT实现更高的回溯和精度,表明本体学相通的组群更加一致和较少混合.

blocks.en: Across most majors, SMI achieves high recall, suggesting that codes within each major are concentrated in a dominant cluster rather than scattered across multiple clusters. In particular, SMI reaches recall above 80% for most ICD major categories, including Endocrine & metabolic, Blood diseases, Mental disorders, Nervous system & sense organs, Circulatory system, Respiratory system, Digestive system, Genitourinary system, Skin, Musculoskeletal, Congenital anomalies, and External causes. Moreover, SMI also achieves high precision for many majors, including 100% precision for Infectious & parasitic, Neoplasms, Mental disorders, Musculoskeletal, Congenital anomalies, Symptoms & ill-defined, and External causes. This indicates that the dominant clusters for these majors are highly pure and contain few codes from other majors.
blocks.zh: 在大多数主要领域,SMI都取得了很高的召回率,表明每个主要领域内部的代码集中在一个主导集群,而不是分散在多个集群中。 特别是,大多数ICD主要类别,包括内分泌和代谢、血液疾病、精神紊乱、神经系统和感官器官、循环系统、呼吸系统、消化系统、基因系统、皮肤、肌肉骨骼、先天性异常和外因,都达到80%以上。 此外,SMI还实现了许多大类的高精度,包括传染病和寄生虫、肿瘤、精神紊乱、肌肉骨骼、先天异常、症状和不明原因以及外因的精度100%。 这表明,这些大类的主导集群非常纯正,包含其他大类的代码很少.

blocks.en: In contrast, BioBERT exhibits lower precision across most majors, implying stronger mixing of majors within the dominant clusters even when recall is moderate. We also observe a few challenging categories where precision remains low despite high recall, such as Blood diseases, Skin, and Injury & poisoning. This suggests that K-means tends to group these categories with clinically or semantically related categories, leading to mixed dominant clusters. Despite this difficulty, SMI still achieves higher recall and precision than BioBERT for these categories. Overall, the results indicate that hierarchy-aware concept representations form clusters that are more consistent with medical ontologies.
blocks.zh: 相比之下,BioBERT在大多数主要项目中表现的精度较低,这意味着即使在召回幅度不大的情况下,主要项目在主要组群中更紧密地混合。 我们还观察到一些挑战性类别,尽管召回率很高,精确度仍然很低,例如血液疾病、皮肤和伤害与中毒。 这表明K-意指倾向于将这些类别与临床或模拟相关类别相分类,从而导致混合优势集群. 尽管存在这一困难,SMI对于这些类别仍然比BioBERT实现更高的回想和精确度. 总体来看,结果显示分级意识概念表述形成与医学本体学更相符合的集群.

blocks.en: Figure 8: Cluster assignment heatmaps for ICD diagnosis embeddings. Rows denote ICD major disease categories and columns denote K-means clusters ordered by their dominant major category. Each cell shows the percentage of codes from a major category assigned to a cluster. Compared with BioBERT, SMI exhibits a stronger diagonal pattern, indicating better alignment between embedding structure and ICD major categories.
blocks.zh: 图8:集束任务热图,用于ICD诊断嵌入. 行表示国际疾病分类主要疾病类别,列表示按主要主要类别订购的K-指组。 每个单元格显示分配给一个集群的主要类别的代码的百分比。 与BioBERT相比,SMI呈现出更强的对角图案,表明嵌入结构与ICD主要类别之间更加一致.

blocks.en: E.4 Details about Rare Code Prediction
blocks.zh: E.4 稀有代码预测的细节

blocks.en: To benchmark drug recommendation on rare ATC codes, we construct a new MIMIC-IV subset. We select five-level ATC codes with 10–20 occurrences, yielding 98 unique long-tailed medications, and restrict drug recommendation to this label space. Because rare targets are extremely sparse, the previous threshold-based metrics (AUPRC, F-score, and Jaccard) are less informative; instead, we evaluate retrieval quality using Recall@15, i.e., whether the true medication labels appear within the top-15 prediction set.
blocks.zh: 为了以稀有ATC代码为基准提出药物建议,我们构建出一个新的MIMIC-IV子集. 我们选择了5级的ATC代码,有10–20起,产生98种独特的长尾药,并将药物推荐限制在这个标签空间. 由于罕见的目标极其稀少,先前的基于阈值的度量衡(AUPRC, F- score, 和Jaccard)信息较少;相反,我们使用Recall@15来评价检索质量,即真实的药物标签是否出现在前15个预测集中.

blocks.en: E.5 Details about Distribution shift
blocks.zh: E.5 分配转移的细节

blocks.en: We assess cross-hospital distribution shift following prior work by learning a hospital-specific density model on patient embeddings and measuring the log-likelihood gap between in-domain samples and samples from other hospitals [ Zhu et al., 2025 ] . We trained a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) as a density estimator on patient embeddings from the eICU dataset [ Kingma and Welling, 2013 ] . For each source hospital k k , we encoded diagnoses and medications using either SMI or BioBERT, and then trained a VAE density estimator p k ​ ( x k ) p_{k}(x_{k}) on the embeddings x k x_{k} from hospital k k . We quantified the distribution shift from source hospital k k to target hospital t t by computing their difference of log-likelihoods: Δ = 𝔼 x k ​ [ log ⁡ p k ​ ( x k ) ] − 𝔼 x t ​ [ log ⁡ p k ​ ( x t ) ] \displaystyle\Delta=\mathbb{E}_{x_{k}}\left[\log p_{k}(x_{k})\right]-\mathbb{E}_{x_{t}}\left[\log p_{k}(x_{t})\right] (6) where log ⁡ p k ​ ( x k ) \log p_{k}(x_{k}) and log ⁡ p k ​ ( x t ) \log p_{k}(x_{t}) are the log - likelihoods of in - domain samples x k x_{k} and out - of - domain samples x t x_{t} evaluated under the VAE trained on k k -th hospital, respectively. A large Δ \Delta implies greater cross-hospital shift between source and target distributions. We approximate the log-likelihood log ⁡ p k ​ ( x ) \log p_{k}(x) using an Importance Weighted Autoencoder (IWAE) objective by drawing K = 64 K=64 importance samples z i ∼ q ⁡ ( z ∣ x ) z_{i}\sim q(z\mid x) [ Burda et al., 2015 ] : log ⁡ p k ​ ( x ) ≈ log ⁡ ( 1 K ​ ∑ i = 1 K p ⁡ ( x , z ( i ) ) q ⁡ ( z ( i ) ∣ x ) ) \displaystyle\log p_{k}(x)\approx\log\left(\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}\frac{p(x,z^{(i)})}{q(z^{(i)}\mid x)}\right) (7) Fig. 9 visualizes cross-hospital distribution shift as the absolute log-likelihood difference ( | Δ | |\Delta| ) between each source-target hospital pair using a hospital specific density model trained on the source. SMI yields consistently lower | Δ | |\Delta| across source–target hospital pairs than BioBERT, indicating better cross-site stability and reduced domain shift. This improvement likely comes from injecting expert-curated medical hierarchies, which place semantically related concepts closer in the embedding space. In contrast, BioBERT relies mainly on textual similarity and does not explicitly encode clinical ontology relationships, leading to larger cross-hospital variability. Overall, SMI effectively mitigates cross-hospital distribution shift and is more suitable for multi-institutional settings with heterogeneous data.

SMI的产量一直低于BioBERT, 这种改进可能来自注入专家精准的医疗等级,这些等级将与精密相关的概念放在嵌入空间中。 相形之下,BioBERT主要依靠文字相似性,并且没有明确编码临床本体关系,导致更大的跨医院可变性. 总体而言,SMI有效缓解了跨医院分布转移,更适合多机构设置,数据不一.

blocks.en: The reviewers of your paper will be asked to use the checklist as one of the factors in their evaluation. While [Yes] is generally preferable to [No] , it is perfectly acceptable to answer [No] provided a proper justification is given (e.g., error bars are not reported because it would be too computationally expensive” or “we were unable to find the license for the dataset we used”). In general, answering [No] or [N/A] is not grounds for rejection. While the questions are phrased in a binary way, we acknowledge that the true answer is often more nuanced, so please just use your best judgment and write a justification to elaborate. All supporting evidence can appear either in the main paper or the supplemental material, provided in appendix. If you answer [Yes] to a question, in the justification please point to the section(s) where related material for the question can be found.

blocks.en:
1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and introduction state the main scope and contributions of SMI, including training-free hierarchy-aware concept representation, theoretical SNR analysis, experimental contributions including relation prediction, downstream clinical prediction, and cross-hospital robustness. These claims are supported by the methodology, theory, and experiments reported in the paper. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The conclusion discusses the scope and limitations of SMI, including its focus on expert-curated coding systems such as ICD and ATC, the need for additional ontology validation and code mapping for emerging disease classifications, newly introduced drugs, and local coding standards. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper states the assumptions and formal theoretical results in Section 3.3 . Complete proofs and supporting derivations are provided in Appendix B . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper describes the datasets, ontology construction, data splits, tasks, metrics, baselines, and evaluation protocols in the main text and appendix. These details provide sufficient information to reproduce the main empirical results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [No] Justification: The paper uses public but credentialed-access clinical datasets, including MIMIC-IV and eICU, whose redistribution is restricted by data-use agreements. We provide implementation details in the appendix, but the current submission does not include an anonymized code release. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper specifies the clinical prediction tasks, evaluation metrics, data splits, baselines, and implementation details in Section 4.1 , 4.4 and 4.5 , with additional baseline and experimental details in Appendices D.4 , E.2 , and E.5 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The clinical prediction results report mean and standard error from bootstrap, while the deterministic relation prediction experiments use threshold selection via grid search and are reported without variance. The paper reports statistical significance tests for drug recommendation, rare drug prediction, and cross-hospital distribution shift. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All experiments were conducted on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU with 96GB memory. SMI is training-free and only requires a one-time computation of frozen LM embeddings, after which the embeddings are reused in downstream tasks. Therefore, SMI introduces minimal additional hardware or computational overhead. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The study uses de-identified, credentialed-access clinical datasets and does not involve intervention on patients, crowdsourcing, or collection of new human-subject data. We found no deviation from the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper discusses positive impacts through improved representation of long-tailed clinical concepts, better clinical prediction, and robustness to cross-site distribution shift. It also discusses deployment-related risks, including dependence on correct ontology selection, local code mapping, and clinician validation before real-world use. The study uses de-identified clinical datasets and does not release patient-level data. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not release a high-risk AI model or dataset. The clinical datasets used in the study are controlled-access and governed by their original data-use agreements.
item[] Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper cites the original sources for existing datasets (i.e., MIMIC-IV, eICU), medical ontologies (i.e., ICD, CCS), language models (i.e., BioBERT), and baseline methods. Access to MIMIC-IV and eICU follows their official credentialed-use requirements. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We plan to release the precomputed SMI concept embeddings and the code for constructing them from public medical ontologies and frozen biomedical LM encoders. We will provide documentation describing the embedding construction procedure, required ontology resources, and usage instructions for downstream tasks. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing, user studies, participant recruitment, or direct interaction with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The study uses de-identified, controlled-access EHR datasets and does not collect new human-subject data or interact with participants. Dataset access is governed by the original data-use agreements. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: The core method uses a frozen biomedical language model encoder, BioBERT, to obtain level-specific clinical code embeddings. The paper describes this usage in the methodology. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.

1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明: 抽象和入门陈述了SMI的主要范围和贡献,包括无培训的分级意识概念代表,理论SNR分析,实验贡献包括关系预测,下游临床预测,和跨医院稳健性. 这些索赔得到文件中报告的方法、理论和实验的支持。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明: 结论讨论了SMI的范围和局限性,包括它侧重于诸如ICD和ATC等由专家验证的编码系统,需要为新出现的疾病分类进行额外的肿瘤学验证和代码映射,新引进的药物,以及当地的编码标准等. • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果该办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响该方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[是] 说明: 文件在第3.3节中说明了假设和正式理论结果。 附录B提供了完整的证明和佐证。 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 • 所有假设均应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明: 论文在正文和附录中描述了数据集,肿瘤构造,数据分化,任务,度量,基线,以及评价协议等. 这些细节为复制主要经验成果提供了充分的信息。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 答复:理由: 本文使用公开但具有信誉的临床数据集,包括MIMIC-IV和ECU,其再分配受到数据使用协议的限制. 我们在附录中提供了执行细节,但本次提交未包括匿名代码发布. · 答案[N/A]是指纸张不包括需要密码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为了保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 文件在第4.1、4.4和4.5节中具体规定了临床预测任务、评价指标、数据分解、基线和执行细节,附录D.4、E.2和E.5中提供了额外的基线和实验细节。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件的核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告的错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验的统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 临床预测结果报告出自靴子的平均值和标准误差,而决定性关系预测实验则使用通过网格搜索选择的阈值,并报告无差异. 文件报告了药物推荐的统计意义测试,稀有药物预测,以及跨医院分布的转变. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是好的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-相格马出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 所有实验都是在具有96GB内存的NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU上进行的. SMI是无培训的,只需要一次性地计算被冻结的LM嵌入物,之后再将嵌入物再用于下游任务. 因此,SMI引入了最低限度的额外硬件或计算间接费用. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 文件应披露整个研究项目是否比文件所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如,初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入文件)。 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 该研究使用去识别,认证的临床数据集,不涉及对患者的干预,众包,或收集新的人主体数据. 我们发现没有偏离新IPS道德守则。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和负面社会影响? 答复:[是] 说明: 论文通过改进长尾临床概念的表述,更好的临床预测,以及稳健的跨地分布转变来讨论积极影响. 报告还讨论了与部署有关的风险,包括依赖正确的本体学选择、本地代码映射和临床医生在现实世界使用之前的验证。 该研究使用去识别的临床数据集,不发布患者层次数据. · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件不讨论社会影响。 二. 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(如:造谣、制造假相、监视)、公平考虑(如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以使人们能训练出能更快生成Deepfake的模型. ^ 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而可能造成的损害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行严格公布,在攻击之外提供防御,监测滥用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布滥用风险高的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或被刮去的数据集)而采取的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文没有发布高风险AI模型或数据集. 研究中使用的临床数据集是可控存取的,并受其原始数据使用协议所规范.
项目[] 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放有可能被滥用或双重用途的已释放模型时,应采取必要的保障措施,允许控制地使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 二. 支助 从互联网上取出的数据组可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明他们如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有者,是否适当记名,是否明确提到并适当遵守许可证和使用条件? 答复:[是] 说明: 本文列举了现有数据集(即MIMIC-IV、eICU)、医学本体学(即ICD、CCS)、语言模型(即BioBERT)和基线方法的原始来源。 进入MIMIC-IV和eICU遵循其官方认证使用要求. • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用了哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证的名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应当包括每项资产. 二. 支助 对于来自某一特定来源(例如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产被放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于受欢迎的数据集,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 他们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 二. 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果不在网上提供这种信息,鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,与资产一起提供的文件是否充分? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们计划从公共医学本体学和冷冻生物医学LM编码器中 释放预编译的SMI概念嵌入和构建这些概念的代码. 我们将提供文件,说明嵌入式施工程序、所需的肿瘤资源以及下游任务的使用说明。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放出新的资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板通报数据集/代码/模型的细节,作为其提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 文件应讨论是否以及如何从资产被使用的人那里获得同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL , 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 与人类主题有关的众包和研究 关于与人类主体的众包实验和研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示和(如果适用的话)截图的全文,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不涉及众包,用户研究,参与者招聘,或与人主体直接互动. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 将这些资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人文主题,那么应在正文中尽可能详细。 二. 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或等同的人类学科研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向研究对象披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得的同等批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 该研究使用解识别,可控存取的EHR数据集,不收集新的人主体数据或与参与者互动. 数据集访问由原始数据使用协议管辖. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 研究对象的研究可能需要IRB批准(或同等批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在文件中明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大相径庭,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 二. 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包含任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。 16. LLM使用宣言问题: 论文是否描述了LLMS的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作、编辑或格式化目的,而且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要申报。 答复:[是] 说明: 核心方法使用被冷冻的生物医学语言模型编码器"BioBERT"来得到同级临床代码嵌入. 文件介绍了这种方法的用法。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The abstract and introduction state the main scope and contributions of SMI, including training-free hierarchy-aware concept representation, theoretical SNR analysis, experimental contributions including relation prediction, downstream clinical prediction, and cross-hospital robustness. These claims are supported by the methodology, theory, and experiments reported in the paper.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The conclusion discusses the scope and limitations of SMI, including its focus on expert-curated coding systems such as ICD and ATC, the need for additional ontology validation and code mapping for emerging disease classifications, newly introduced drugs, and local coding standards.
blocks.zh: 说明: 结论讨论了SMI的范围和局限性,包括它侧重于诸如ICD和ATC等由专家验证的编码系统,需要为新出现的疾病分类进行额外的肿瘤学验证和代码映射,新引进的药物,以及当地的编码标准等.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
blocks.zh: • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果只在几个数据集上或用几个运行来测试这种做法。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社区完整性的准则方面起重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。

blocks.en: Theory assumptions and proofs
blocks.zh: 理论假设和证明

blocks.en: Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
blocks.zh: 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper states the assumptions and formal theoretical results in Section 3.3 . Complete proofs and supporting derivations are provided in Appendix B .
blocks.zh: 说明: 文件在第3.3节中说明了假设和正式理论结果。 附录B提供了完整的证明和佐证。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.
blocks.zh: 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 • 所有假设均应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results.

blocks.en: Experimental result reproducibility
blocks.zh: 实验结果可复制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper describes the datasets, ontology construction, data splits, tasks, metrics, baselines, and evaluation protocols in the main text and appendix. These details provide sufficient information to reproduce the main empirical results.
blocks.zh: 说明: 论文在正文和附录中描述了数据集,肿瘤构造,数据分化,任务,度量,基线,以及评价协议等. 这些细节为复制主要经验成果提供了充分的信息。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果.

blocks.en: Open access to data and code
blocks.zh: 开放对数据和代码的访问

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material?
blocks.zh: 问题: 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示?

blocks.en: Answer: [No]
blocks.zh: 答复:[无]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper uses public but credentialed-access clinical datasets, including MIMIC-IV and eICU, whose redistribution is restricted by data-use agreements. We provide implementation details in the appendix, but the current submission does not include an anonymized code release.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.

blocks.en: Justification: The paper specifies the clinical prediction tasks, evaluation metrics, data splits, baselines, and implementation details in Section 4.1 , 4.4 and 4.5 , with additional baseline and experimental details in Appendices D.4 , E.2 , and E.5 .

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material.

blocks.en: Experiment statistical significance
blocks.zh: 实验统计意义

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸质报告错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The clinical prediction results report mean and standard error from bootstrap, while the deterministic relation prediction experiments use threshold selection via grid search and are reported without variance. The paper reports statistical significance tests for drug recommendation, rare drug prediction, and cross-hospital distribution shift.
blocks.zh: 说明: 临床预测结果报告出自靴子的平均值和标准误差,而决定性关系预测实验则使用通过网格搜索选择的阈值,并报告无差异. 文件报告了药物推荐的统计意义测试,稀有药物预测,以及跨医院分布的转变.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布出的错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是好的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-相格马出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格.
